Judgment

1 The present Civil 1st Appeal has been preferred by the appellant- State against the judgment and decree dated 12.08.2017 passed by the Court of learned Principal District Judge, Kathua (for short 'trial Court') in a suit titled 'Reva Devi and others vs. State and others' whereby the trial Court has awarded Rs.23,0500/- as compensation for death of deceased Yash Pal Singh along with 6% interest w.e.f 05.09.2011 till realization.

entities.text: Reva Devi and others vs. State and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. The facts, in brief, leading to filing of this appeal are that the respondents herein filed a suit on 23.07.2011 claiming to be the indigent persons.

The said suit was entertained in the 'forma papuris'
and in terms of order dated 05.09.2011, the trial Court declared the respondents as indigent persons on the report of concerned officer of the Court.
The respondents claimed a sum of Rs.3500000/-(thirty five lac) by applying the principles of Motor Vehicle Accident Act under different heads.
The suit was resisted by the appellant-State herein.
It was stated by the appellant before the trial Court that the State is not responsible in any manner for the fatal accident.

The trial Court after hearing the parties held that an accident has occurred which has resulted into death of deceased Yash Pal Singh due to electrocution by the sheer negligence of the appellant-State and the appellant-State was found to pay damages under the principle of strict liability.

The Trial Court,
after weighing the evidence, vide its order dated 12.08.2017 has awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.23,05,000/-to the respondents herein.

The relevant extract of the said order reads thus:

1 "the plaintiffs for the aforestated reasons are, thus, entitled compensation on the following counts:
1. Loss of dependence: Rs.19,80,000/-
2. Loss of consortium: Rs.1,00000/-
3. Loss of love, care and affection: Rs.2,00,000/-
4. Funeral expenses: Rs.25000/-

sentences.text: Mr. Amit Gupta learned AAG appearing for the appellant-State after arguing for some time, restricted his arguments with regard to reduction of quantum of compensation on the head 'loss of consortium' and 'loss of love, care and affection' granted by the trial Court.

He has contended that in terms of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co.
Ltd Vs Pranay Sethi & ors reported as 2017 AIR (SC) 5157, the learned trial Court erred in granting compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium and further erred in granting compensation of Rs. 2,00,000/- towards loss of love, care and affection and the same is to be calculated @ Rs. 40,000/- per legal heir.
4.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co.
Ltd Vs Pranay Sethi & ors reported as 2017 AIR (SC) 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents/claimants fairly submits that in terms of the dictam of the Honble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), grant of compensation under the head 'Love and Affection' has to be deducted from the total amount of compensation awarded by the learned trial Court, however, the grant of compensation under the head 'Loss of Consortium' is fixed @ Rs. 40,000/-.

5. The arguments raised by the learned counsel for the parties are purely legal and based on the law settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (supra), which has held as under:-
"
As far as the conventional heads are concerned, we find it difficult to agree with the view expressed in Rajesh.

It has granted Rs. 25,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.
1,00,000/- loss of consortium and Rs. 1,00,000/- towards loss of care and guidance for minor children.
The head relating to loss of care and minor children does not exist.
Though Rajesh refers to Santosh Devi, it does not seem to follow the same.
The conventional and traditional heads, needless to say, cannot be determined on percentage basis because that would not be an acceptable criterion.
Unlike determination of income, the said heads have to be quantified.
Any quantification must have a reasonable foundation.
There can be no dispute over the fact that price index, fall in bank interest, escalation of rates in many a field have to be noticed.

The State vs Reva Devi And Others on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30428653/
2 court cannot remain oblivious to the same.

entities.text: State vs Reva Devi And Others on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There has been a thumb rule in this aspect.

Otherwise, there will be extreme difficulty in determination of the same and unless the thumb rule is applied, there will be immense variation lacking any kind of consistency as a consequence of which, the orders passed by the tribunals and courts are likely to be unguided.
Therefore, we think it seemly to fix reasonable sums.

It seems to us that reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs. 15,000/-, Rs. 40,000/- and Rs.
15,000/- respectively.
The principle of revisiting the said heads is an acceptable principle.
But the revisit should not be fact-centric or quantum-centric.

We think that it would be condign that the amount that we have quantified should be enhanced on percentage basis in every three years and the enhancement should be at the rate of 10% in a span of three years.

We are disposed to hold so because that will bring in consistency in respect of those heads".
6.

From the perusal of the aforesaid Judgment, it is abundantly clear that, for the conventional head,
namely, 'Loss of Consortium', the amount of compensation is fixed at Rs. 40,000/-.

With regard to the head 'loss of love, care and affection' the Hon'ble Supreme Court in New India Assurance Company Limited Versus Smt. Somwati and others (2020) 9 SCC 644 after considering Pranay Sethi's case (supra) has held that "loss of love and affection" is comprehended in "loss of consortium", therefore, there is no justification to award compensation towards "loss of love and affection" as a separate head.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited Versus Smt. Somwati and others (2020) 9 SCC 644
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, in view of the law laid down, the trial Court was not justified in awarding Rs.2:00 lac towards 'loss of love, care and affection'.
The same is, accordingly, deducted from the total amount of compensation awarded by the trial Court.

7. In view of above, the impugned judgment and decree dated 12.08.2017 is modified to the following extent:
Loss of Consortium which is granted as Rs.1,00,000/- and loss of love and affection which is granted as Rs.200,000/- by learned trial Court is modified as Rs.40,000x3=
Rs.1,20,000/- to be paid to the respondents/claimants.
8.

Accordingly, the computation of compensation by the learned trial Court is modified as detailed below:
Loss of dependent: Rs.19,80,000/-
Loss of consortium: Rs.1,20,000/-
Funeral expenses: Rs.25000/-
Total: Rs.21,25,000/-
State vs
Reva Devi And Others

on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30428653/
3 9.
It is stated by the learned counsel for the respondents that in terms of order dated 31.07.2018, the awarded amount has already been deposited before the Registry of this Court.
Registry is directed to release the awarded amount in terms of this judgment along with interest accrued thereon in favour of the respondents herein within a period of four weeks.
The differential amount may be released in favour of the appellant/State.
Appeal stands disposed of accordingly.
(MOKSHA KHAJURIA KAZMI) JUDGE Jammu 13 .12.2023 Sanjeev
